keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. A 15 km circle around Rabat (about 700 km2) is the smallest the grid can draw for a 0.91 km2 city state; the page gives no frontier. The Dila'iya suzerainty of 1641-1661 and the Alawite submission of 1668 do not change the shape.

region.text: Salé and the Kasbah of Rabat on the Bou Regreg

ledger.note: April 1627: the Hornacheros of Rabat and Salé form a corsair republic. 'In April 1627 the Hornacheros expelled the Sherif's governor and constituted themselves a virtually independent republic', with Sidi al-Ayachi's support; infobox 'Established 1627'.

region.text: Salé and Rabat on the Bou Regreg

ledger.note: June 1668: Moulay al-Rashid ends the republic. 'Sultan Moulay al-Rashid of the Alawite dynasty defeated the Dilaites and ended the republic's independence'; the Alawi page: he 'forced Salé and its pirate republic to acknowledge his authority' (undated). Infobox 'Disestablished 1668'.

wars.name: Hornacheros' coup at Salé

zones.text: Salé and the Kasbah of Rabat

wars.outcome: The Hornacheros expelled the Sherif's governor in April 1627 and made themselves a virtually independent republic; John Harrison negotiated a treaty with Sidi al-Ayachi in May.

wars.name: Civil strife between Andalusians and Hornacheros
wars.outcome: Clashes ended in 1630 with a 16-member Diwan split between Andalusians and Hornacheros; fighting resumed in 1636-1637 and English ships bombarded the Kasbah in 1637; in 1631 the Hornacheros sent a draft treaty offering the city to Philip IV's monarchy.

wars.name: Dila'iya hegemony over Salé
wars.outcome: In 1641 the Zawiya Dila'iya 'imposed a religious hegemony over Salé and its parent republic'; the infobox has the republic under Dila'iya suzerainty 1641-1661; Salé rose against the Dila'ite governor in 1660 and was lost to the Zawiya in 1661 (Dila page); the republic was at war with the Zawiya in the early 1660s.

wars.name: Alawite conquest of the Bou Regreg
wars.outcome: Moulay al-Rashid defeated the Dilaites in June 1668 and ended the republic's independence; Salé 'acknowledged his authority'.
wars.note: The Alawi page does not date Salé's submission; the Republic of Salé page gives June 1668.

certainty.note: A walled city state: the two cities on the Bou Regreg are the whole territory; no outer frontier exists.

notes: Cliopatria has no Bou Regreg row. The Saadi dossier (af-02-e) lists this state as a successor on the admin1 'Rabat - Salé - Zemmour - Zaer' and has no 1627 loss; the Alawi (morocco) dossier lists it as a predecessor and records the Dila'iya, not the republic, as holder of Salé in 1641, so the Saadi shape still contains Salé until 1641 while this dossier founds the republic in 1627: the integrator can resolve the overlap by giving the cells to the republic from 1627. The Dila'iya dossier of this batch records the vassal relation 1641-1661 with this state as counterpart. The page does not describe a Dutch alliance (only Jan Janszoon as Grand Admiral from 1624 and a Dutch consul from 1643) and does not mention Moulay Ismail or 1666. The 1609 Morisco influx, the 1614 first governor Brahim Vargas and Janszoon's 1624 admiralty precede the state and are not entered. No governor is listed for 1642-1650. Gazetteer: Rabat resolves.
